# Shi Group at the University of Toledo

> Physics-informed AI for Polymer and Biomacromolecule Modeling and Design.

The Shi Group is led by Jiale Shi, Assistant Professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering at the University of Toledo in Toledo, Ohio, USA. We are a fully computational (dry) lab developing AI methods, including generative models, language models, AI for science foundation models, and graph learning. Experimental work and validation are carried out by collaborators outside the group, including the UToledo Polymer Institute.

## Research

- Conditional generative models for complex polymer design.
- Environment-aware AI models for complex polymer property and response prediction.
- AI models to accelerate and interpret complex polymer simulation.
- Physics-informed AI for biomacromolecules, combining polymer physics and statistical physics to understand and design proteins, RNA, and lipid nanoparticles (LNPs).

Application interests include semiconductors, healthcare, sustainability, energy, and gas separation.

## Representative publications and code

- [Measuring Differences in Protein Allosteric Graphs Constructed via Molecular Dynamics Simulations](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.6c00082): Jiale Shi, Zhongyi Wan, Renjie Zhu, Qiang Cui. J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2026, 22, 12, 6180-6195. [Code](https://github.com/shijiale0609/Distance_Protein_Dynamics).
- [MacroSimGNN: Efficient and Accurate Calculation of Macromolecule Pairwise Similarity via Graph Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.macromol.5c03015): Jiale Shi, Runzhong Wang, Nathan J. Rebello, Jiarui Lu, Debra J. Audus, Bradley D. Olsen. Macromolecules 2026, 59, 4, 1885-1900. [Code](https://github.com/shijiale0609/MacroSimGNN).
